Reasoning: Taking the CD direction as 0°, then the CB direction is 180°. From ∠DCE=60°, the CE direction is 60°; from ∠ACB=45°, the included angle between CA and CB is 45°, so the CA direction is 180°−45°=135°. If CM bisects $\angle BCE$ and CN bisects $\angle DCA$, as shown in Figure 2, what is the measure of $\angle MCN$?

method.method_draft: Use absolute ray directions from the straight baseline in Figure 2. First read from the image that B, C, D form a straight horizontal line, with CB pointing left and CD pointing right; CA is the up-left ray, CE is the up-right ray, and CM and CN are the indicated angle bisectors. From the text, ∠ACB = 45° and ∠DCE = 60°. Since CB and CD are opposite rays, take CD as direction 0° and CB as direction 180°. Then CE has direction 60°, and CA has direction 180° − 45° = 135°. Because CM bisects ∠BCE, its direction is halfway between 180° and 60°, namely 120°. Because CN bisects ∠DCA, its direction is halfway between 0° and 135°, namely 67.5°. Therefore ∠MCN is the difference between these two directions: 120° − 67.5° = 52.5°.
